problem: Rewrite the statement $¬((¬P∧¬Q)∨(P∧¬Q))$ using De Morgan's laws.

examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Statement Using De Morgan's Laws
examples.problem:
Simplify the statement $
eg ( (P \lor 
eg Q) \land (Q \lor 
eg P) )$ using De Morgan's laws.
examples.worked_solution:
De Morgan's laws state that

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(P∧Q)≡¬P∨¬Q, \\ ¬(P∨Q)≡¬P∧¬Q.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬((P∨¬Q)∧(Q∨¬P)) & ≡¬(P∨¬Q)∨¬(Q∨¬P) \\  & ≡(¬P∧¬(¬Q))∨(¬Q∧¬(¬P)) \\  & ≡(¬P∧Q)∨(¬Q∧P)\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
$\,$ $-1$ is not negative or ${-1}$ is not empty.

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
feedback.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B.
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(-1\text{ is not negative}\text{ or }{-1}\text{ is not empty}) & ≡¬((-1\text{ is not negative})\,∨\,({-1}\text{ is not empty})) \\  & ≡¬(-1\text{ is not negative})\,∧\,¬({-1}\text{ is not empty}) \\  & ≡(-1\text{ is negative})\,∧\,({-1}\text{ is empty}) \\  & ≡-1\text{ is negative}\text{ and }{-1}\text{ is empty}.\end{aligned}
$$
